about: One image series for the blog (krizaka-blog#193): chapter N continues chapter N-1. Prompts and seeds only; the pictures live on Bunny, never here. Made with Orazaka's media worker (mflux, FLUX.2 [klein] 4B, Apache-2.0) on the Mac, no paid API.
style: Flat vector illustration in the Krizaka brand style: simple geometric shapes, clean outlines, soft gradients, no photographic texture. Deep indigo and violet night sky fading to dark ink, a large warm orange sun disc, faint blue constellation lines with round nodes, cyan and magenta dots, layered triangular mountains with thin bright edges, a dark curved ground line. No people, no text, no lettering, no logos.
continuity: Same valley, same sun and mountains as the previous picture, same camera, same palette: keep everything already built and add only the new element. Only the birds named below appear, each exactly once; no human figures anywhere.

chapters.beat: The first picture: the empty valley at dusk, Montreal rooftops as simple geometric silhouettes on the ground line, one orange falcon with a visor alone on the tallest roof, watching.

A small workshop hut now stands beside the rooftops, its window glowing and a glowing hexagon on its door; a table outside holds only a laptop-shaped lantern; the one falcon sits alone on the hut's roof.

A violet owl arrives and weighs on a brass balance scale a glowing picture frame against stacks of coins, beside a glowing stove-like machine (the GPU) with steam. Exactly one owl, standing next to the scale, and exactly one orange falcon with a dark visor on the roof of the right hut.

A small film set on the hillside: a projector throwing a wide beam on a hanging screen, a rail with a camera. The single violet owl perches on top of the screen and watches the beam; the single orange falcon with a dark visor stands on the ground at the left. Only these two birds.

The red duck with glasses sits at a pottery wheel under a canopy that shapes three vessels of the same clay: a tall phone shape, a tablet shape and a wide laptop shape; the falcon stands at the left, the owl on the canopy.
Two new houses by the stream, one with a scroll of law pinned in the window and one with a small shop awning and a hanging basket; lamps lit, a footbridge between them.
A gate with a latch on the footbridge, one wing open, one closed; a checklist board with ticks beside it and an empty basket on the gate post.
A pink flamingo arrives; thirty small typewriter-like machines glow in rows in a long night shed, each with a tiny lamp, keys locked in a strongbox outside.
A drafting table at the valley's edge with a large audit report sheet and a big magnifying glass over the settlement; two lanterns of different colors lean over it.
A long winding path up the hill drawn as a climbing curve with many small flags along it, a few flags checked and a clay tennis court with painted lines at the curve's foot.
A train of small hexagon crates rolling along rails through a row of lit checkpoint gates toward a lighthouse on a Mediterranean harbour; gates glow green.

A workshop of nineteen small colored building blocks on shelves, a chisel and a mallet resting on one block, a basketball hoop on a post at the court's edge, a souk's horseshoe arches with zellige patterns behind. Nobody is in the picture but the birds.

Colored cables run from the workshop hut to many small houses like a patchbay, a big control tower with a rotating beacon, a booth with two turntables and crates of vinyl records under sweeping light beams.
A small desk by the first hut, a lamp, and a net of fine nets catching bugs right at the desk before they reach the road; limestone cliffs of the Chartreuse behind.
A blue pigeon arrives and flies a sealed envelope over a row of dashboard gates, a barometer dial showing a green zone beside a sky-blue cloud tower. Each of the five birds appears exactly once.

The whole settlement at night in full glow, all five birds standing together in a row, each exactly once (falcon, owl, duck, flamingo, pigeon), a ruler and a gauge standing in front measuring the village.
